title: Home Mortgage Loans: Mortgage Insurance Premium Rates by Program
content:
# Home Mortgage Loans: Mortgage Insurance Premium Rates by Program

For Home Mortgage Loans, the insurance that protects the lender is priced differently in each program. This schedule shows the one-time premium financed into the loan, the yearly premium collected in monthly pieces, the original loan-to-value above which private mortgage insurance attaches, and, for the FHA program, the number of years the annual premium runs when the loan started at a low enough loan-to-value.

## How to read each figure

- **Upfront premium** — for FHA, the upfront mortgage insurance premium; for VA, the funding fee. Either is financed into the loan and is quoted as a percentage of the base loan amount.
- **Annual premium** — a yearly percentage of the principal balance, billed in monthly installments.
- **PMI attaches above** — private mortgage insurance is required when the loan-to-value at origination is greater than this percentage. Programs without private mortgage insurance show "not applicable".
- **FHA annual premium term** — the number of years the FHA annual premium is paid when the original loan-to-value was 90 percent or lower; when it was higher, the premium is paid for the whole life of the loan. Only the FHA program has a figure here.

| Program | Upfront premium (% of base amount) | Annual premium (% of principal balance) | PMI attaches above original LTV of (%) | FHA annual premium term (years, original LTV 90% or lower) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FHA 30-Year Fixed Mortgage | 1.75 | 0.55 | not applicable | 11 |
| VA 30-Year Fixed Mortgage | 2.15 | 0.00 | not applicable | not applicable |
| Conventional 30-Year Fixed Mortgage | 0.00 | 0.46 | 80 | not applicable |
| Conventional 15-Year Fixed Mortgage | 0.00 | 0.32 | 80 | not applicable |
| 7/6 SOFR Adjustable-Rate Mortgage | 0.00 | 0.46 | 80 | not applicable |
| Jumbo 30-Year Fixed Mortgage | 0.00 | 0.00 | not applicable | not applicable |

## Questions this schedule answers

**Which programs finance a one-time premium?** The FHA program, at 1.75 percent, and the VA program, whose funding fee is 2.15 percent; the other four finance nothing upfront.

**Which programs carry no annual premium?** The VA program and the jumbo program both show 0.00.

**Hypothetical arithmetic.** On an imagined FHA base loan amount of $200000.00, an upfront premium of 1.75 percent comes to $3500.00, found by multiplying the base amount by 1.75 and dividing by 100. The loan amount in this example is invented for illustration.
